docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Irbis workflows usually start by loading data, checking the visualization settings, and saving the project as an .irbis file.

Start here:

  • Load data
  • View raw planes data
  • Create a primary 3D model
  • Export processed data as an .irbis file

For a complete model workflow, follow Import -> Reconstruct -> Track dendrite -> Separate spines -> Export results.

docs.title: Irbis file structure
docs.text:
This page describes the main structure of an Irbis output file.

Detailed table column definitions are described on separate reference pages.

docs.title: Structure overview
docs.text:
• Irbis file
  • info
  • timeline
  • tools
  • views
  • results
  • planes
  • tracks
  • points
  • model

docs.title: Info
docs.text:
General metadata describing the Irbis file, version, dataset identity, units and save history.

  • info.irbisVersion (double) - Irbis version used to create the file.
  • info.matlabVersion (char) - MATLAB version used to create the file.
  • info.groupName (char)
  • info.round (double)
  • info.cell (double)
  • info.dish (double)
  • info.description (char)
  • info.experimentDate (datetime)
  • info.notes (char)
  • info.spaceUnits (char) - Units used for spatial measurements in the dataset.
  • info.timeUnits (char) - Units used for temporal measurements in the dataset.
  • info.path (char) - Path to the working directory where file was saved (rewritten during saving).
  • info.filename (char) - Filename of the saved Irbis file (rewritten during saving).
  • info.createTimestamp (datetime) - Timestamp when the structure was initially created.
  • info.saveTimestamp (datetime) - Timestamp when the structure was last saved (rewritten during saving).

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
Structure for managing time points, current selections, and time-dependent indices.

  • timeline.nTimePoints (double) - Number of time points present in the dataset.
  • timeline.currentTimePoint (double) - Currently selected time point index.
  • timeline.currentIndex.planes (double / array) - Index of the currently selected plane for each time point.
  • timeline.currentIndex.tracks (double / array) - Index of the currently selected track for each time point.
  • timeline.currentIndex.points (double / array) - Index of the currently selected point for each time point.
  • timeline.currentIndex.model (struct) - Per-branch indices of currently selected model objects for each time point.
  • timeline.currentIndex.tools.areas (double / array) - Index(es) of the currently selected area tool entries.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Storage for user-defined tools and annotations, such as area selections.

  • tools.areas (struct) - Storage for area-selection tool entries.
  • tools.areas.List (cell / table) - List/table of area tool entries.
    • See: areas table

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
Storage for viewer configurations, camera positions, and related settings.

  • views.storedViewsList (table) - Stored viewer configurations and camera positions.
    • See: views table

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Not used atm.

  • results (struct) - Placeholder for results and computed outputs.

docs.title: Planes
docs.text:
Storage for structural image data, image stack parameters and spatial reference settings.

  • planes.refOrigFileName (char) - Original filename of the reference image.
  • planes.zstack (array / numeric) - Raw image data (z-stack), shape xyztch.
  • planes.pixel_size (double) - Pixel size in spatial units.
  • planes.z_spacing (double) - Z-step spacing for z-stack images.
  • planes.channelNames (cell) - Channel names list (e.g., {'GFP','Homer','DIC'}).
  • planes.channelColors (cell) - Per-channel color specifications.
  • planes.channelColormaps (cell) - Per-channel colormap settings.
  • planes.channel_ranges (cell) - Per-channel histogram ranges for plotting.
  • planes.imSize (double) - Single-plane XY size in pixels.
  • planes.nPlanes (double) - Number of Z planes in a stack.
  • planes.nChannels (double) - Number of channels in the dataset.
  • planes.nTimePoints (double) - Number of time points in the image data.
  • planes.bitDepth (double) - Bit depth of the image data (e.g., 8,16,32).
  • planes.spacialRef (imref2d) - Spatial referencing object for 2D images.
  • planes.refImParam.depth (double) - Default reference image depth (z plane) used for registration.
  • planes.refImParam.channel (double) - Channel index used as reference image.
  • planes.timeDrift (numeric) - Measured time drift applied to plane images (per time point).

docs.title: Tracks
docs.text:
Storage for trajectories (loaded from the TrackMate files) and their parameters.

  • tracks.tracksOrigFileName (cell) - Original filenames for track input per time point.
  • tracks.nTracks (cell) - Number of tracks found per time point.
  • tracks.nFrames (cell) - Number of frames per time point.
  • tracks.frameInterval (cell) - Frame interval in temporal units (per time point).
  • tracks.group (cell) - Group identifier for tracks per time point.
  • tracks.description (cell) - Descriptive text for track sets per time point.
  • tracks.driftCorrection (cell) - Drift correction parameters applied to tracks per time point.
  • tracks.timeRange (cell) - Time range information for tracks per time point.
  • tracks.tracksList (cell) - Cell array of track tables, one per time point.
    • See: tracks table
  • tracks.filterTable (cell) - (Deprecated) Filter tables per time point.
  • tracks.storedFilters (FilteringStorage) - Storage object for filters applied to tracks.
  • tracks.storedCategorizations (CategorizationStorage) - Storage object for categorizations related to tracks.
  • tracks.storedSummarizedTables (SummarizedTableStorageClass) - Storage for precomputed summarized tables for tracks.
  • tracks.timePointPresent (logical) - Flag indicating whether tracks include explicit time-point information.

docs.title: Points
docs.text:
Storage for detected points and corresponding metadata.

  • points.pointsList (table) - Table/list of detected or stored points.
    • See: points table
  • points.fileName (char) - Source filename for points data.
  • points.registration (struct) - Registration parameters for points relative to images.
  • points.manualAlignment (struct) - Manual alignment adjustments applied to points.
  • points.storedSummarizedTables (SummarizedTableStorageClass) - Storage for summarized tables derived from points.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Storage for branch-based model objects, object parameters, reconstruction settings and drift correction data.

  • model.branches (cell) - Names of model branches available in this dataset.
  • model.selectableBranches (cell) - Subset of branches that are selectable in the UI.
  • model.(branch).Color (double (1x3)) - RGB color for objects in this branch.
  • model.(branch).Transparency (double) - Transparency (alpha) for objects in this branch.
  • model.(branch).Show (logical / numeric) - Visibility flag for this branch in the viewer.
  • model.(branch).List (cell array of tables) - Cell array where each cell contains a table of objects for the time point defined by currentIndex in this branch. The table structure depends on the reconstruction method and branch type.
    • See: model table
  • model.(branch).methodApplied (char) - Reconstruction method applied to derived objects in this branch.
  • model.(branch).storedFilters (FilteringStorage) - Stored filters for objects in this branch.
  • model.(branch).storedCategorizations (CategorizationStorage) - Stored categorizations for objects in this branch.
  • model.(branch).storedSummarizedTables (SummarizedTableStorageClass) - Summarized tables storage for objects in this branch.
  • model.timeDrift (double) - Time-dependent drift vectors for the model (nTimePoints x 3).
  • model.timeDriftCorrected (logical / numeric) - Flag indicating if time drift correction has been applied.
  • model.driftCorrectedColumns (cell) - List of model property names that are corrected by drift compensation.

docs.title: Object features
docs.text: This page describes mesh-derived object features calculated by ObjectFeatureExtractor.

docs.title: volume
docs.text:
• Meaning: signed-tetrahedra mesh volume magnitude (enclosed volume)
  • Formula: V = |sum(dot(cross(v1, v2), v3))| / 6 over all faces
  • Units: unit^3 (for example um^3)

docs.title: surface
docs.text:
• Meaning: total area of all mesh triangles
  • Formula: A = 0.5 * sum(norm(cross(v2 - v1, v3 - v1))) over all faces
  • Units: unit^2 (for example um^2)

docs.title: averageDistance
docs.text:
• Meaning: average distance from basePoint p to vertices v_i
  • Formula: mean(||v_i - p||)
  • Units: unit (for example um)

docs.title: euclideanLength
docs.text:
• Meaning: robust estimate of maximal spine extent from base point
  • Formula: mean(top 5% of ||v_i - p||)
  • Units: unit (for example um)

docs.title: distanceCoefficientOfVariation
docs.text:
• Meaning: relative spread of vertex distances from base point
  • Formula: std(d_i)/mean(d_i), where d_i = ||v_i - p||
  • Units: dimensionless

docs.title: sphericity
docs.text:
• Meaning: compactness relative to a sphere (1 = perfect sphere)
  • Formula: (pi^(1/3) * (6V)^(2/3)) / S
  • Units: dimensionless

docs.title: convexHullVolume
docs.text:
• Meaning: volume of the convex hull enclosing all vertices
  • Formula: second output of convhull(x, y, z)
  • Units: unit^3 (for example um^3)

docs.title: solidity
docs.text:
• Meaning: fraction of convex hull occupied by object volume
  • Formula: V / V_hull
  • Units: dimensionless

docs.title: openAngle
docs.text:
• Meaning: average angular spread of vertex directions from base point
  • Units: degrees

docs.title: baseToTipAngle
docs.text:
• Meaning: orientation of the base patch relative to the main axis of the object
  • Formula: angle between the normal vector at the base point and the vector from base point to the mean of the 5% furthest vertices (tip point)
  • Units: degrees

docs.title: basePatchArea
docs.text:
• Meaning: surface area of the patch where the spine is cut from the shaft
  • Formula: sum of areas of faces in base patch
  • Units: unit^2 (for example um^2)

docs.title: Step-by-step guides
docs.text: These pages convert the Irbis manual into short task-focused workflows. Each page keeps the prerequisites, UI location, and related next steps close to the instructions.

docs.title: Common tutorial flows
docs.text:
• Import -> Reconstruct -> Track dendrite -> Separate spines -> Export results
  • Importing data only

docs.text:
• Data import and saving
  • Planes processing
  • 3D model processing
  • Tracks processing

docs.title: Data import and saving
docs.text:
Use these pages to open raw data, open existing .irbis projects, and save processed data.

  • Load data
  • Export processed data as an .irbis file

Related workflows:

  • Continue from import to view raw planes data.
  • Continue from import to view tracks.

docs.title: Load data
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Raw volumetric data, TrackMate tracks, or processed data in .irbis format.

UI location:

  • Main app: Files tab.
  • Alternative raw-data tabs: Planes, Points, or Tracks.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In the Files tab, press New.
  2. Choose the data type: Import planes, Import tracks, or Load .irbis structure.
  3. In the file dialog, select the file and press Open.

docs.title: Alternative: new raw data
docs.text:
1. For structural microscopy images supported by BioFormats, go to the Planes tab.
  2. For SMLM data, go to the Points tab.
  3. For TrackMate trajectory XML files, go to the Tracks tab.
  4. Press Import at the bottom of the selected tab.
  5. Select the data file and press Open.

docs.title: Alternative: existing Irbis data
docs.text:
1. Press Load .irbis file.
  2. Select the .irbis file and open it.

If you repeatedly use files from the same folder:

  1. Select the folder from the folder drop-down menu.
  2. If the folder is missing, press Add path and select it.
  3. Double-click the folder in the drop-down menu.
  4. Double-click a file in the file list to load it.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• For structural images, continue to View raw planes data.
  • For TrackMate data, continue to View tracks.
  • Save your work with Export processed data as an .irbis file.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the Files tab with New, Load .irbis file, Add path, and the file list visible.

docs.title: Export processed data as an .irbis file
docs.text:
Exporting data as an .irbis file lets you reopen the processed project in Irbis later.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Data loaded or processed in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Files tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. If needed, fill in metadata in the File info section.
  2. Press Save as .irbis.
  3. Select the output folder.
  4. Enter a file name.
  5. Press Save.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Start a project with Load data.
  • Export object tables from Select objects and export results.

Screenshot placeholder

docs.title: 3D model processing
docs.text:
3D reconstruction is currently based on planes data.

  • Create a new model
  • Create a primary 3D model
  • Detect drift and correct it
  • Register objects across time points
  • Track a dendrite
  • Generate the dendritic shaft
  • Separate spines from the shaft
  • Select objects and export results
  • Manually adjust selected objects

Tutorial:

  • Import -> Reconstruct -> Track dendrite -> Separate spines -> Export results

docs.title: Create a new model
docs.text:
Create an empty model structure before generating model parts, unless you loaded data that already contain a model.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to the Model tab.
  2. Press Create model at the bottom of the page.
  3. Confirm that the model-generation options are now visible.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Create a primary 3D model.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the Model tab before and after Create model is pressed.

docs.title: Detect drift and correct it
docs.text:
If all time points are generated at once during 3D reconstruction, drift correction runs automatically.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Primary 3D model created for all time points.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Full subtab.
  • Sections: Drift correction and Position adjustment tool.

docs.title: Detect drift
docs.text:
1. In Drift correction, press Detect drift.
  2. By default, the first time point is used as reference.
  3. If needed, select a different reference type from the reference drop-down menu.
  4. After drift is detected, check Drift correction to apply correction.

docs.title: Manually adjust drift
docs.text:
1. Check Show reference.
  2. In Position adjustment tool, set the switch to Drift.
  3. Select the movement step.
  4. Use the arrows to align the model with the reference for the current time point.
  5. If the drift is far off, use the red reset buttons in the middle of the arrows. One resets x-y, and the other resets z.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Register objects across time points.

Video placeholder

Add a short clip showing Detect drift, enabling Drift correction, and manual arrow adjustment.

docs.title: Generate the dendritic shaft
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Primary 3D model created for all time points.
  • Time drift corrected.
  • Primary 3D model registered in time.
  • Dendrite tracked.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Dendrite subtab.
  • Sections: Shaft generation and adjustment and, if used, Adaptive shaft settings.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the shaft generation method from the drop-down menu.
  2. Use Constant diameter to approximate the shaft as a tube with circular cross-section, or elliptical cross-section when z scale is not 1.
  3. If desired, check Parallel computing. This can speed calculations, but startup may take some time.
  4. Press Generate shaft.
  5. If All time points is checked in Dendrite tracking, the shaft is generated for all time points. Otherwise, it is generated only for the current time point.
  6. Adjust shaft diameter with the Radius slider.
  7. To apply the diameter to all time points, check Same radius for all time points.
  8. For the Constant diameter model, adjust z scale if needed. A value of 1 is circular; higher values make the cross-section more rectangular.
  9. For the Adaptive shaft model, tune parameters in Adaptive shaft settings.
  10. Press Test one plane to check adaptive model accuracy before applying settings broadly.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Separate spines from the shaft.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Shaft generation and adjustment with method, Parallel computing, Generate shaft, Radius, Same radius, and z scale visible.

docs.title: Manually adjust selected objects
docs.text:
Use object context menus to correct registration, divide merged objects, redefine spines, delete objects, or attach objects at the registration level.

Before you start

UI location:

  • Visualization panel.
  • Open the context menu by left-clicking an object, then right-clicking it.

docs.title: Select objects
docs.text:
1. Go to the tab for the object type you want to edit.
  2. Left-click an object to select it.
  3. Hold Ctrl while left-clicking to select multiple objects.
  4. Right-click a selected object to open the context menu.

Only objects of the currently selected tab are selectable. Selected objects change color.

Context menu actions labelled Single apply only to the right-clicked object. Actions labelled Multi apply to all selected objects.

docs.title: Single: select next
docs.text:
Use this to connect an object with its match in the next time point.

  1. Click Single: Select next.
  2. Irbis moves to the next time point.
  3. Left-click the corresponding object.

docs.title: Single: select previous
docs.text:
Use this to connect an object with its match in the previous time point.

  1. Click Single: Select previous.
  2. Irbis moves to the previous time point.
  3. Left-click the corresponding object.

docs.title: Single: divide
docs.text:
Use this when one reconstructed object contains two merged objects.

  1. Click Single: Divide.
  2. Move, rotate, and resize the cutting plane so it delineates the desired cut.
  3. Press Enter when satisfied.
  4. If Enter does not work, click inside the plot and press Enter again.
  5. To cancel while the plane is visible, press Esc. If needed, click inside the plot first.
  6. If the cut is wrong, press Undo in the bottom-right corner.

docs.title: Single: redefine
docs.text:
This is available only for spines. It changes where a spine is separated from the dendritic shaft.

  1. Click Single: Redefine.
  2. Move and rotate the cutting cylinder so it corresponds to the shaft.
  3. Press Enter when satisfied.
  4. If Enter does not work, click inside the plot and press Enter again.
  5. To cancel while the cylinder is visible, press Esc. If needed, click inside the plot first.
  6. If the result is wrong, press Undo in the bottom-right corner.

docs.title: Multi: delete
docs.text:
1. Click Multi: Delete.
  2. Irbis deletes all selected objects in the current time point.

docs.title: Multi: delete in all time points
docs.text:
1. Click Multi: Delete in all time points.
  2. Irbis deletes selected objects in all time points where the corresponding group IDs exist.

docs.title: Multi: attach
docs.text:
Use this when objects of the same type should not be separated, such as protrusions separated from the main body by imperfect reconstruction.

  1. Click Multi: Attach.
  2. When prompted, click the main body to connect the selected objects to.

This does not form a geometric connection; objects are connected at the registration level.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Use Register objects across time points before manual registration corrections.
  • Use Separate spines from the shaft before redefining spine separation.

Video placeholder

Add clips for Divide, Redefine, Delete, and Attach context-menu actions.

docs.title: Create a primary 3D model
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.
  • Model structure created.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Full subtab, 3D reconstruction section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the channel of interest from the channel drop-down menu.
  2. Set the threshold that separates background from signal.
  3. Press Show to preview the selected area highlighted in gray.
  4. If required, choose More time points and set First and Last used time point.
  5. Select reconstruction detail level from 1 to 5. Level 1 is fastest and least detailed. Level 5 is most detailed and computationally demanding.
  6. If needed, adjust Advanced reconstruction settings.
  7. Confirm that pixel size and z-spacing are correct in the Planes tab.
  8. Press Generate 3D and wait for reconstruction to finish.

docs.title: Threshold for constant signal
docs.text:
1. Press Auto for automatic threshold estimation.
  2. Or set the threshold manually in the spinner.
  3. Press Show to check the selected area.

If signal strength is stable, define the threshold for one time point. Irbis uses the same value for the rest.

docs.title: Threshold for bleaching signal
docs.text:
1. Open Advanced reconstruction settings.
  2. Check Bleaching compensation.
  3. Set the threshold for the first and last time point.
  4. If the switch is set to Selected range, compensation applies only between the selected first and last time point. Only those time points have editable thresholds.
  5. Check the bleaching compensation value next to the checkbox.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Detect drift and correct it.
  • Then Register objects across time points.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Full > 3D reconstruction with threshold, Show, Advanced reconstruction settings, and Generate 3D visible.

docs.title: Register objects across time points
docs.text:
Use registration to match individual dendrite models between time points.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Primary 3D model created for all time points.
  • Time drift corrected.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Full subtab, Object list section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Open Object list.
  2. Review the list of individual dendrite models. Each spatially separated object appears as a separate item.
  3. Press Register.
  4. Check registration by selecting an object in the list or visualization window and moving through time points.
  5. Confirm that the object keeps the same group ID, shown in brackets next to the model.
  6. If registration is wrong, increase the recognition limit next to Register.
  7. Press Register again to apply the changed limit.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Track a dendrite.
  • Use Manually adjust selected objects if automatic matching needs correction.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Object list with Register and group IDs visible.

docs.title: Select objects and export results
docs.text:
Objects can be selected with a left click. When selected, the spine ID and group ID in brackets appear next to the object. Additional object information appears in green in the upper-left corner of the visualization panel.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • 3D model created.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, subtab for the desired object type.
  • Visualization panel.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to the object-type subtab you want to examine.
  2. Expand Object list.
  3. Select an object by clicking its number in the list, or by left-clicking it in the visualization panel.
  4. Use the object list to check object IDs and group IDs.
  5. Press Plot time points to open an external plot of object development over time.
  6. Press Export to xls to create an XLS file with volume and surface development for each object.

Objects in different time points are connected by group ID.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Use Manually adjust selected objects to edit object registration or object geometry.
  • Use ResultsViewer for table and plot exploration.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot showing selected object labels, Object list, Plot time points, and Export to xls.

docs.title: Separate spines from the shaft
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • 3D model created.
  • Dendrites tracked.
  • Dendritic shaft model generated.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Spines subtab, Spine separation section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Go to Model > Spines.
  2. To generate the model for all time points, check All time points.
  3. Press Separate spines.
  4. When prompted, left-click the shaft used to separate spines.
  5. Wait for separation to finish.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Select objects and export results.
  • If a spine split needs correction, use Manually adjust selected objects.

Video placeholder

Add a clip showing shaft selection and the resulting separated spines.

docs.title: Track a dendrite
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Primary 3D model created for all time points.
  • Time drift corrected.
  • Primary 3D model registered in time.

UI location:

  • Main app: Model tab, Dendrite subtab, Dendrite tracking section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. To track the dendrite for every time point, check All time points.
  2. Press Track dendrite.
  3. Select the object to track by clicking it.
  4. When planes data appear, left-click one end of the dendrite.
  5. Left-click the other end of the dendrite.
  6. If tracking fails at a time point, select the start and end points again when prompted.
  7. To exit selection, press Esc.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Generate the dendritic shaft.

Video placeholder

Add a clip showing dendrite end-point selection on planes data.

docs.title: Planes processing
docs.text:
Planes are structural microscopy images with at least two dimensions, xy. To create a 3D model, the planes data must be at least 3D, such as a z-stack.

  • View raw planes data
  • Align planes across time points
  • Crop planes
  • Preprocess planes
  • Adjust channel histogram
  • Delete or save planes data

Related workflows:

  • After planes are ready, continue to Create a new model.

docs.title: Adjust channel histogram
docs.text:
This changes only visualization. It does not change the raw data.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab, histogram controls at the bottom.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the editable channel by clicking its channel-name button in Channels.
  2. At the bottom of the tab, drag the edge of the colored rectangle to change the displayed range.
  3. Press Auto to adjust the range automatically.
  4. Press Reset to return to the default view.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• For data-changing adjustments, use Preprocess planes.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the channel histogram controls.

docs.title: Align planes across time points
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab, Pre-processing section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Pre-processing, click Pre-register.
  2. Review the window showing the calculated shift between the first time point and each following time point.
  3. Press Accept to apply the shifts.

Irbis shifts each time point and crops the hanging edges.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Check raw data first with View raw planes data.
  • Continue cleanup with Crop planes or Preprocess planes.

Video placeholder

Add a short clip showing Pre-register and Accept.

docs.title: Crop planes
docs.text:
Cropping lets you analyze a subset of the image and can reduce processing requirements.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab, Pre-processing section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Pre-processing, click Crop.
  2. In the new window, adjust the red outline around the area you want to keep.
  3. Press Crop.
  4. To cancel, press Cancel.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• After cropping, continue to Preprocess planes or Create a primary 3D model.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the crop window with the red outline visible.

docs.title: Delete or save planes data
docs.text:
Planes data are saved inside the .irbis file unless you delete them. You can also export planes as TIFF files.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab, bottom of the tab.

docs.title: Delete planes data
docs.text:
Use this after 3D reconstruction if you no longer need planes data and want to save space or improve performance.

  1. Click Delete planes.
  2. In the confirmation dialog, select Yes.
  3. Alternatively, select Yes, but keep copy as *.mat to save a MATLAB-only copy.

docs.title: Save planes as TIFF
docs.text:
1. Click Save planes as tif.
  2. Select the output folder.
  3. Enter the file name.

Warning

Each channel is saved in a separate TIFF file, and most metadata are lost.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Save the full project with Export processed data as an .irbis file.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Delete planes and Save planes as tif.

docs.title: Preprocess planes
docs.text:
Preprocessing is applied only to the currently editable channel.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Planes data loaded in Irbis.
  • Editable channel selected in the Planes tab.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab, Pre-processing section.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. In Pre-processing, click the settings icon button.
  2. In the preprocessing window, activate the methods you want to use by clicking their method buttons, such as Spatial filter.
  3. If needed, change the order: select a method rectangle and move it with the arrows at the bottom of the tab.
  4. Compare the original editable channel on the left with the adjusted data on the right.
  5. When satisfied, press Save settings.
  6. Enter a workflow name in the dialog.
  7. Select the saved pipeline from the drop-down menu.
  8. Press Apply to preprocess the editable channel.
  9. To return to original data, press Reset.

Saved pipelines appear in the preprocessing window and in the main window Filter set drop-down menu.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Check channel selection in View raw planes data.
  • Continue to Create a primary 3D model.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the preprocessing window with original data, adjusted data, method buttons, and Save settings visible.

docs.title: View raw planes data
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Raw data or preprocessed .irbis data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Planes tab.

docs.title: Scroll through the z-stack
docs.text:
1. Change the number in the Plane spinner.
  2. Alternatively, hold Shift and use the scroll wheel.

docs.title: Create a z-projection
docs.text:
1. Change the switch to Projection.
  2. Set Depth. Depth 1 includes the selected plane plus one plane above and one below.
  3. Select the projection mode from the drop-down menu. The default is maximum intensity projection.

docs.title: Select channels to view
docs.text: 1. Tick the checkboxes for the channels you want to show.

docs.title: Select the editable channel
docs.text:
1. In Channels, press the button with the channel name.
  2. The greyed-out channel button marks the currently editable channel.

docs.title: Check pixel size and z-step
docs.text:
1. In Tools, check pixel size and z step.
  2. Correct these values if needed. They should load from image metadata, but checking them is recommended.
  3. Adjust z step if you need to correct spherical aberration in the raw data.

docs.title: Show helper elements
docs.text:
1. Tick Scale bar in Tools to show a scale bar.
  2. Tick Box to show a red bounding box around the planes plot. This helps confirm whether planes are visible.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Improve alignment with Align planes across time points.
  • Reduce the region with Crop planes.
  • Continue to Create a new model.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the Planes tab with Plane, Projection, Depth, Channels, pixel size, z step, Scale bar, and Box visible.

docs.title: ResultsViewer
docs.text:
ResultsViewer is part of Irbis for exploring generated data in tables and plots. It supports filtering and custom groups.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Processed model or tracks data.

UI location:

  • ResultsViewer window.
  • Open it from the right side of the bottom panel by pressing the plot icon button.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• Left side: parameter selection and table.
  • Right side: plots, filtering, and categorization.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
• All parameters mode pools data from all time points; table columns are parameters.
  • Selected parameter mode shows one parameter across time; columns are time points and rows are objects connected by group ID.

Pages:

  • Use modes and plots
  • Filter available data
  • Define ResultsViewer categorization
  • Use batch mode

Warning

Filters and categorizations are synced between the main Irbis app and ResultsViewer, but generated data itself is not. If you change or generate data in the main app, close and reopen ResultsViewer to sync changes.

docs.title: Use ResultsViewer in batch mode
docs.text:
Batch mode lets you explore data from multiple datasets together.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • One or more .irbis files with processed data.

UI location:

  • ResultsViewer window.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Batch load.
  2. Select all files you want to open.
  3. Wait for the datasets to load.

Warning

Batch loading can be computationally demanding and may take time.

Warning

Loading multiple datasets severs the connection with the main Irbis app. Uploaded data, filters, and categorizations are reset and are no longer synced.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Use Use ResultsViewer modes and plots after loading batch data.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Batch load and the loaded combined table.

docs.title: Define ResultsViewer categorization
docs.text:
Irbis-generated data can be further categorized in ResultsViewer.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Data opened in ResultsViewer.
  • Desired modality selected at the top of ResultsViewer: model, tracks, or points.
  • For model data, desired branch selected at the top of ResultsViewer.

UI location:

  • ResultsViewer: Categorization panel at the bottom right.

docs.title: Define a new categorization
docs.text:
1. In Categorization, press Add new categorization.
  2. In the dialog, enter the categorization name in Categorization name.
  3. Define categories by combining criteria.
  4. Enter each category name in its text field.
  5. Press Add criteria in a category section to add a rule.
  6. Press Add category to add another category.
  7. Press Save categorization.

docs.title: Use categorization templates
docs.text:
Templates are stored categorization rules that can be reused for multiple datasets. Templates are stored with Irbis and loaded in the Template drop-down menu.

  1. To use an existing template, select it from Template and press Use.
  2. To edit an existing template, select it and press Edit.
  3. To create a template, press Add a new template and define it like a categorization.
  4. To transfer templates between computers or users, press Export templates and later use Import templates.
  5. To store an existing dataset categorization as a template, right-click the selected categorization in the parameter checkbox list on the left side of ResultsViewer.

Warning

Filters and categorizations are synced between the main Irbis app and ResultsViewer, but generated data itself is not. If you change or generate data in the main app, close and reopen ResultsViewer to sync changes.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Track categorizations are described in Define and edit track categorizations.

Screenshot placeholder

Add screenshots of Add new categorization, Template controls, and Export templates.

docs.title: Filter available data
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Data opened in ResultsViewer.
  • Desired modality selected at the top of ResultsViewer: model, tracks, or points.
  • For model data, desired branch selected at the top of ResultsViewer.

UI location:

  • ResultsViewer: Filtering panel on the left.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Select the parameter to filter by from the drop-down menu.
  2. For categorical parameters, select included categories in the checkbox list.
  3. For numerical parameters, set the lower and upper filter range.
  4. For numerical parameters, you can also set the range in the plot.
  5. Press Filter.
  6. Existing filters appear as state buttons in the Filtering panel.
  7. Toggle a filter button off to disable the filter. Toggle it on to enable it again.
  8. To delete a filter, select the parameter name from the drop-down menu and press delete.

Filters should sync with the main Irbis app. Changing a filter in Irbis updates ResultsViewer, and changing it in ResultsViewer updates Irbis.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Use Use ResultsViewer modes and plots to inspect filtered data.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the Filtering panel with a numerical and categorical filter.

docs.title: Use ResultsViewer modes and plots
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • Data opened in ResultsViewer.

UI location:

  • ResultsViewer window.

docs.title: All parameters mode
docs.text:
1. Switch to All parameters mode.
  2. Select parameters from the checkbox list on the left.
  3. Review the table. Each column is a parameter, and data from all time points are pooled.

docs.title: Selected parameter mode
docs.text:
1. Switch to Selected parameter mode.
  2. Select the desired parameter.
  3. Review the table. Each column is one time point and each row is one object connected in time by a single group ID.

Warning

Only model parts connected with group ID can be shown in Selected parameter mode.

docs.title: Plot data
docs.text:
1. Click one or more selected table columns.
  2. Select the plot type from the drop-down menu in the upper-right corner.
  3. If more parameters are selected than the plot type supports, only the last selected parameters are shown.
  4. In Selected parameter mode, switch between individual lines and the average of selected lines.
  5. Tick categorical as labels to group plot data by categories.

Supported plot types include histograms, bar plots, scatter plots, and line plots.

In All parameters mode, plots usually use the whole table column, even if only some rows are selected. Exceptions include plot types such as individual: line.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Narrow the table with Filter available data.
  • Create groups with Define ResultsViewer categorization.

Screenshot placeholder

Add screenshots of All parameters mode, Selected parameter mode, and the plot type drop-down menu.

docs.title: Tracks processing
docs.text:
Tracks are single-molecule tracking microscopy data. Irbis currently accepts processed tracks from TrackMate in .xml format.

  • Import tracks
  • View tracks
  • Calculate track parameters
  • Define and edit track categorizations

Related workflows:

  • Explore processed track data in ResultsViewer.

docs.title: Calculate track parameters
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • TrackMate .xml data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Tracks tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Calculate parameters.
  2. Wait for all implemented calculations to finish.

This step can take a while.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Define and edit track categorizations.
  • Explore results in ResultsViewer.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Calculate parameters in the Tracks tab.

docs.title: Define and edit track categorizations
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • TrackMate .xml data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Tracks tab, Categorization section.

docs.title: Define a simple categorization
docs.text:
Simple categorization is based on one numerical parameter.

  1. Select the parameter from the first drop-down menu in Categorization.
  2. Fill thresholds into th1, th2, and th3.
  3. Use up to three thresholds to create up to four categories.
  4. If you need fewer categories, fill unused threshold fields with values outside the parameter range.
  5. Press Apply.

docs.title: Define a complex categorization
docs.text:
Complex categorizations can combine multiple numerical and categorical parameters.

  1. Press Add categorization.
  2. In the dialog, enter the categorization name.
  3. Define each category in its own box. Two boxes appear by default.
  4. Press Add category to add more categories.
  5. Rename each category in its category-name field.
  6. Add conditions inside each category box. Each condition line contains a parameter, relation, value, and delete button.
  7. Use relations such as equals, lessThan, and greaterThan.
  8. Press Add criteria to add more conditions.
  9. Press Save categorization.

docs.title: Delete a categorization
docs.text:
1. Select the categorization from the drop-down menu.
  2. Press Delete grouping.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• ResultsViewer has a separate Define ResultsViewer categorization workflow.

Screenshot placeholder

Add screenshots of simple thresholds and the Add categorization dialog.

docs.title: Import tracks
docs.text:
Track data can be uploaded as TrackMate .xml files.

Before you start

UI location:

  • Main app: Tracks tab.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Press Import tracks.
  2. In the file dialog, select the XML files to import.
  3. To select multiple files, hold Ctrl while selecting them.
  4. If multiple files are selected, enter the time points they belong to in the window that opens.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to View tracks.
  • Then Calculate track parameters.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Import tracks and the time-point assignment window.

docs.title: View tracks
docs.text:
Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • TrackMate .xml data loaded in Irbis.

UI location:

  • Main app: Tracks tab.

docs.title: Change tracks visualization
docs.text:
1. Adjust Line thickness to change trajectory thickness in pixels.
  2. Adjust Tail to change how many past frames are displayed in the trajectory.
  3. Check Limit to plane to collapse trajectories to the z-position of the current plane.
  4. Check Limit to area to show only trajectories within existing areas. This applies only if areas exist.

docs.title: Change color-coding
docs.text:
1. In the first Colorcode drop-down menu, select the parameter used for color-coding.
  2. In the second Colorcode drop-down menu, select the colormap.
  3. Select random to color trajectories randomly, independent of parameter values.
  4. Check or uncheck colorbar to show or hide the colorbar in the bottom-right corner of the plotting area.

docs.title: Filter visible tracks
docs.text:
1. Press Filter to show filtering options.
  2. Select the filtering parameter from the drop-down menu.
  3. For numerical parameters, use the histogram to set the visible range.
  4. For categorical parameters, select visible categories from the checkbox list.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Continue to Calculate track parameters.
  • Then Define and edit track categorizations.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of Tracks visualization controls, Colorcode controls, Filter, histogram, and category checkboxes.

docs.title: Viewport, animation, and shortcuts
docs.text:
Use these pages to navigate the visualization panel, manage views, and create animations.

  • Navigate the visualization panel
  • Use keyboard shortcuts
  • Create animations
  • Save views

docs.title: Create animations
docs.text:
Use animation options to set keyframes and play transitions between saved views.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • 3D model created.

UI location:

  • Main app: Viewport tab, Animation options section.

docs.title: Build an animation
docs.text:
1. Position the view as desired.
  2. Press Add keyframe.
  3. Repeat for all views between which transitions should occur.
  4. To remove keyframes, select them in the listbox and press Delete selected. Use Ctrl+click to select multiple keyframes.
  5. To reorder keyframes, select them and use the up and down arrows beside the listbox.
  6. To change a selected keyframe to the current view, select it and press Change for current.
  7. To change a transition, select the first keyframe in the pair, adjust Duration, and press Apply to selected.
  8. To inspect a saved keyframe view, double-click it in the listbox or click its line in the animation timeline.
  9. Press Play animation.
  10. To animate only selected keyframes, tick Selected only.

During playback, each keyframe first switches time point and visible components, then applies special animation if selected, then runs the transition.

docs.title: Add special animations
docs.text:
1. Select an effect from Special effect.
  2. Press Add.

The Expand spines option expands spines away from the dendritic shaft.

docs.title: Save and load animation setup
docs.text:
1. Press Save script to save the keyframe setup.
  2. Press Load script.
  3. In the dialog, select the saved setup and press Open.

The keyframe setup can be saved and applied to another model.

docs.title: Preview spine expansion
docs.text:
1. Press Expand spine view.
  2. Press Reset view to return to the default position.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Save static views with Save views.

Video placeholder

Add a video showing Add keyframe, Duration, Play animation, and Expand spines.

docs.title: Shortcuts
docs.text:
• Shift + scroll wheel: scroll through z-planes.
  • Ctrl + scroll wheel: scroll through time points.

Warning

Ctrl + scroll wheel may not work in the current MATLAB version.

docs.title: Related
docs.text: • See mouse controls in Navigate the visualization panel.

docs.title: Navigate the visualization panel
docs.text:
Before you start

UI location:

  • Main visualization panel.
  • Bottom panel under the visualization panel.

docs.title: Mouse controls
docs.text:
• Hold right mouse button: rotate in 3D.
  • Hold scroll wheel button: translate.
  • Scroll wheel: zoom.
  • Color wheel button: expand options for hiding or showing model parts and changing color and transparency settings.
  • Home: reset axes view.

docs.title: Bottom panel
docs.text:
• Data-type checkboxes: show or hide currently present data types.
  • Reset: reset the view, useful when zoom or rotation gets stuck.
  • Undo and Redo: undo or redo supported steps.
  • Export figure: export the current view into a separate window that can be saved.
  • Plot icon button: open ResultsViewer.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Learn shortcuts in Use keyboard shortcuts.
  • Store camera setups with Save views.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the visualization panel bottom controls.

docs.title: Save views
docs.text:
Saved views store the rotation and zoom of the axes and the selection of visible elements. The current time point is not saved.

Before you start

Prerequisites:

  • 3D model created.

UI location:

  • Main app: Viewport tab, View storing option section.

docs.title: Save and use a view
docs.text:
1. Position the view as desired.
  2. Select the components you want visible.
  3. In View storing option, press Store view.
  4. Double-click the saved view name in the listbox to apply it.
  5. To rename a view, select it and press Rename view.
  6. To delete a view, select it and press Delete view.

docs.title: Show only selected objects
docs.text:
1. Select the objects to keep visible by left-clicking them.
  2. Use Ctrl+click to select multiple objects.
  3. Use the show-only-selected option in View storing option to hide all other objects.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Use Create animations when you need transitions between views.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of View storing option with Store view, Rename view, and Delete view.

docs.title: Tutorial: import, reconstruct, track, separate, export
docs.text: This is the main end-to-end flow for structural microscopy data.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Load data.
  2. View raw planes data and verify pixel size and z-step.
  3. Optional: Align planes across time points, Crop planes, or Preprocess planes.
  4. Create a new model.
  5. Create a primary 3D model.
  6. Detect drift and correct it.
  7. Register objects across time points.
  8. Track a dendrite.
  9. Generate the dendritic shaft.
  10. Separate spines from the shaft.
  11. Select objects and export results.
  12. Save the project as an .irbis file.

Screenshot placeholder

Add a screenshot of the finished Model tab with separated spines visible.

Video placeholder

Add a short walkthrough of the full sequence from import to export.

docs.title: Tutorial: importing data
docs.text:
Use this tutorial when you only need to get data into Irbis and save the project.

  1. Load data.
  2. If you loaded planes, check View raw planes data.
  3. If you loaded TrackMate XML files, check Import tracks and View tracks.
  4. Save the project with Export processed data as an .irbis file.
